acceptance.note: Both PRs merged fast-forward on 2026-11-22: #47 at 55efbf6 (12:36Z) and #54 at 5e2bb99 (15:07Z). Coordinator ruling: the floor is revised and studies get no extra base motion. The coordinator approved EC-1a's design (the union covers only layers declaring neither events nor flicker); EC-A kept the flicker weight at 0 (64 near-still cases probed: every defect that reaches 8 bits already fails through the ratio, and weight 0.1 fails a correct near-still flicker layer). An all-episodic scene has no floor and passes only when its wrap is also exactly 0; any non-episodic layer keeps the old guard; fire@1 declares flicker but moves continuously, and a near-still fire still fails through motion-in. The plan's section 8.1 keeps its original bullet and gains a dated revision paragraph. Left for owners: acceptance/m1 R3 stands, and EC-0's README sentence and the EC-6 and EC-7 criteria's K3 sections follow in their own files.

practice_observation: Splitting the gate change (EC-1a) from the criterion (EC-A) worked as the ruling intended: the reviewer's mutant kernels found six wrong rules that passed all 20 original tests, so the criterion was strengthened before the kernel change was judged by it, and the kernel review found one real gap (the exact-0 pass also held with an empty-region continuous layer). The design note's measurement, that a study's own base motion clears its own floor by 1.9 times once episodic layers are left out, turned a request for extra study motion into a gate revision. The change is small (+284 -13 in the kernel PR) and landed on one CI run.
